cards.front: Area of a triangle
cards.back: 1/2 × base × perpendicular height. Example: base 10 cm, height 6 cm gives 30 cm².
cards.say: Area of a triangle is one half times base times perpendicular height. Example: base ten centimetres, height six centimetres gives thirty square centimetres.

cards.front: Why is a triangle half of a rectangle?
cards.back: Two identical triangles fit together to make a rectangle with the same base and height.
cards.say: Why is a triangle half of a rectangle? Two identical triangles fit together to make a rectangle with the same base and height.

cards.front: Triangle with base 8 cm and height 5 cm: area?
cards.say: Triangle with base eight centimetres and height five centimetres: area? twenty square centimetres. eight times five equals forty, then half of forty is twenty.

cards.front: Triangle with base 12 cm and height 5 cm: area?
cards.say: Triangle with base twelve centimetres and height five centimetres: area? thirty square centimetres. twelve times five equals sixty, and half of sixty is thirty.

cards.front: Right-angled triangle with short sides 6 cm and 8 cm: area?
cards.back: 24 cm². The two short sides are the base and height: 1/2 × 6 × 8 = 24.
cards.say: Right angled triangle with short sides six centimetres and eight centimetres: area? Twenty four square centimetres. The short sides are the base and height, and half of six times eight is twenty four.

cards.front: Does the height of a triangle use the slanted side?
cards.back: No. Use the perpendicular height, which makes a right angle with the base.
cards.say: Does the height of a triangle use the slanted side? No. Use the perpendicular height, which makes a right angle with the base.

cards.front: Area of a parallelogram
cards.back: base × perpendicular height. Example: base 7 cm and height 4 cm gives 28 cm².
cards.say: Area of a parallelogram is base times perpendicular height. Example: base seven centimetres and height four centimetres gives twenty eight square centimetres.

cards.front: Area of a rectangle 3.5 m by 2 m
cards.say: Area of a rectangle three point five metres by two metres. seven square metres. three point five times two equals seven.

cards.front: A compound shape is a 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle with a 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle cut out. Area?
cards.say: A compound shape is a ten by six centimetre rectangle with a four by three centimetre rectangle cut out. Area? Forty eight square centimetres. Sixty minus twelve equals forty eight.

cards.front: Perimeter of a compound shape: how do you find a missing side?
cards.back: Use the known sides. Example: if the whole width is 10 cm and one part is 4 cm, the missing part is 6 cm.
cards.say: Perimeter of a compound shape: how do you find a missing side? Use the known sides. If the whole width is ten centimetres and one part is four, the missing part is six.

cards.front: Volume of a cuboid
cards.back: length × width × height. Example: 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm = 60 cm³.
cards.say: Volume of a cuboid is length times width times height. Example: five centimetres times four centimetres times three centimetres equals sixty cubic centimetres.

cards.front: Volume of a cube with side 5 cm
cards.say: Volume of a cube with side five centimetres. one hundred and twenty five cubic centimetres. five times five times five equals one hundred and twenty five.

cards.front: A cuboid has volume 120 cm³ and a base of 6 cm by 4 cm. Find its height.
cards.back: 5 cm. The base area is 24 cm² and 120 ÷ 24 = 5.
cards.say: A cuboid has volume 120 cubic centimetres and a six by four centimetre base. Find its height. Five centimetres. The base area is twenty four, and one hundred and twenty over that is five.

cards.front: How many mL does 1 cm³ hold?
cards.say: How many millilitres does one cubic centimetre hold? One millilitre.

cards.front: How many cm³ are in 1 litre?
cards.say: How many cubic centimetres are in one litre? One thousand cubic centimetres.

cards.front: A tank measures 50 cm by 20 cm by 10 cm. How many litres can it hold?
cards.say: A tank measures fifty by twenty by ten centimetres. How many litres can it hold? Ten litres. Fifty times twenty times ten is ten thousand cubic centimetres, and that is ten litres.

cards.front: Surface area of a cube with side 3 cm
cards.back: 54 cm². Each face is 3 × 3 = 9 and there are 6 faces.
cards.say: Surface area of a cube with side three centimetres. fifty four square centimetres. Each face is three times three equals nine and there are six faces.

cards.front: Surface area of a 2 cm by 3 cm by 4 cm cuboid
cards.say: Surface area of a two by three by four centimetre cuboid. Fifty two square centimetres. Twelve plus sixteen plus twenty four equals fifty two.

cards.front: How many m² are in 1 km²?
cards.say: How many square metres are in one square kilometre? One million square metres.

cards.front: How many m² in a hectare?
cards.say: How many square metres are in a hectare? Ten thousand square metres, a square of one hundred metres by one hundred metres.

cards.front: Which unit: area, perimeter or volume of a box?
cards.back: Area in cm², perimeter in cm, volume in cm³.
cards.say: Which units: area, perimeter or volume of a box? Area in square centimetres, perimeter in centimetres, volume in cubic centimetres.

cards.front: If you double every edge of a cube, how many times bigger is the volume?
cards.say: If you double every edge of a cube, how many times bigger is the volume? eight times bigger. two times two times two equals eight.

cards.front: A triangle has area 20 cm² and base 8 cm. Find its height.
cards.say: A triangle has area twenty square centimetres and base eight centimetres. Find its height. five centimetres. Double the area: forty. Then forty divided by eight equals five.

cards.front: What is the area of a square with perimeter 20 cm?
cards.say: What is the area of a square with perimeter twenty centimetres? twenty five square centimetres. Each side is twenty divided by four equals five, and five times five equals twenty five.
